newsitem.title: EGYPT: Boutros-Ghali still Africa U.N. candidate - Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Boutros-Ghali still Africa U.N. candidate - Egypt.

text.p: Egypt said on Wednesday that Boutros Boutros-Ghali would remain on Africa's list of candidates for the post of U.N. secretary general even after the United States vetoed a second term for him.

"Boutros-Ghali remains an Egyptian and African candidate and his name is still on the list submitted to the Security Council so we do not need to put forth his name again," Assistant Foreign Minister Sayed el-Masri told reporters.
"Egypt will support him diplomatically and politically," he added.

The 15-member Security Council voted last month by 14 to one to reappoint Boutros-Ghali, but the United States, one of five veto-wielding permanent members, voted against him because it says he has done too little to reform the cash-strapped body.

On Tuesday, Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak told reporters in Tunis that Egypt could do no more to help Boutros-Ghali win a second term at the United Nations. "Our mission has reached its limits after one country vetoed him," he said.
At the United Nations, Mubarak's comments raised concern as to whether Egypt was dropping its campaign to re-elect Boutros-Ghali.

But U.N. spokeswoman Sylvana Foa said Boutros-Ghali had spoken to Mubarak on Tuesday and the Egyptian president said his comments "were taken out of context and that Egypt would continue to support his re-election."
